{{Short description|None}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=December 2020}}
The Scottish Football Association Challenge Cup, commonly known as the [[Scottish Cup]], is a [[Single-elimination tournament|knockout]] cup competition in [[Football in Scotland|Scottish football]]. Organised by the [[Scottish Football Association]], it is the third oldest existing football competition in the world, having commenced in the [[1873–74 in Scottish football|1873–74 season]] just two years after the first [[FA Cup]]. The winners are awarded the world's oldest trophy, minted in 1885.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.scottishcup.org/museum.html|title=Official Site of the Tennent's Scottish Cup ''Scottish Football Museum Experience''|access-date=16 December 2008}}</ref>

[[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] hold the record for most wins with 43, and the most final appearances with 62<!--42 wins, 19 defeats, and 1909 was withheld-->. Celtic are the current holders, having beaten [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]] in the [[2026 Scottish Cup final|2026 final]].

==History==
At the time of the cup's first season [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]] were by far the dominant force in Scottish football, and no other team had even managed to score a goal against them until 1875, eight years after their formation.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Soar|first=Phil|author2=Martin Tyler |title=Encyclopedia of British Football|year=1983|publisher=Willow Books|isbn=0-0021-8049-9|pages=64}}</ref> This early dominance meant they were invited into the [[FA Cup 1871–72|first FA Cup season]] and in season 1883–84 they came close to a cup double, winning the [[Scottish Cup]] but losing the [[FA Cup final]] to [[Blackburn Rovers F.C.|Blackburn Rovers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fchd.info/cups/facup1883-84.htm |title=FA Cup 1883–84 |publisher=The Football Club History Database |access-date=16 December 2008 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100216071759/http://www.fchd.info/cups/facup1883-84.htm |archive-date=16 February 2010 }}</ref> They again met [[Blackburn Rovers F.C.|Blackburn Rovers]] in the following season's final but were defeated once again.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fchd.info/cups/facup1884-85.htm |title=FA Cup 1884–85 |publisher=The Football Club History Database |access-date=16 December 2008 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100216071803/http://www.fchd.info/cups/facup1884-85.htm |archive-date=16 February 2010 }}</ref> Other Scottish teams competed in the [[FA Cup]] such as [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] and [[Third Lanark A.C.|3rd Lanark RV]] and continued to compete until 1887, when the [[Scottish Football Association]] banned its members from taking any further part in the "English Cup".<ref>{{cite web |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/sports_talk/1179349.stm|title=Ask Albert – Number 5|publisher=BBC |work=[[BBC Sport]]|access-date=2 December 2013|date=19 February 2001 |archive-date=28 March 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090328165910/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/sports_talk/1179349.stm}}</ref> By the time the [[Scottish Football League]] was founded in the [[1890–91 in Scottish football|1890–91 season]], [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]] had been eclipsed by many of the league clubs, they finally agreed to enter the competition in the [[1900–01 in Scottish football|1900–01 season]], they finished seventh in their first season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nozdrul.plus.com/zfeweb/scotland/league/tables/level1/sl1901d1.html|title=Scottish League Division One 1900–01|publisher=James Ross|access-date=16 December 2008|archive-date=2 August 2008|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080802045856/http://www.nozdrul.plus.com/zfeweb/scotland/league/tables/level1/sl1901d1.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> Their demise was reflected in their [[Scottish Cup]] results, although they reached four finals after the foundation of the league they could only win one and their 1893 success was their last, reaching only one more final in 1900. [[Dumbarton F.C.|Dumbarton]] filled the void left by [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]] for a time, but like all Scottish football competitions, the [[Scottish Cup]] would come to be dominated by the [[Old Firm]] of [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] and [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]].

In [[1909 Scottish Cup final|1909]] the cup was withheld by the [[Scottish Football Association]] after a riot broke out following a [[Replay (sports)|replay]] between [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] and [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]]. The first match was drawn 2–2 and the second 1–1.<ref name=guardian09>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2007/mar/21/theknowledge.sport|title=Why no one won the Scottish Cup in 1909|work=The Guardian|access-date=16 December 2008 | location=London | first=James | last=Dart | date=21 March 2007}}</ref>

The cup was not competed for between 1914 and 1919 due to [[World War I]]. [[World War II]] prevented competition between 1939 and 1945 although the [[Scottish War Emergency Cup]] was held in the [[1939–40 in Scottish football|1939–40 season]].

A draw in the final used to result in the match being [[Replay (sports)|replayed]] at a later date. Since the 1981 final, however, the result has always been decided on the day, with a [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shoot-out]] if required after [[extra time]].
